payload.friendly_name: Layer merge, pack registration and effective reads
payload.purpose_context: Core needs the service to answer what is in force for a project. After the activation register, the remaining steps of ADR-0055 are the cross-level layer merge on the depends_on resolver, whole-pack registration with full replacement, and the four effective reads (#103) that today answer 501. This mission builds them so a service-v0.x release candidate can follow.
payload.purpose_tldr: The charter service merges built-in, org and project packs, replaces a registered pack whole, and answers what is in force for an activation.

A locked T wins (stays in force, override not applied). A required T does not block: required means T or an override/enhancement of it must be in force, so an active E overriding T satisfies the requirement and hides T.
Retry up to 3 times; a stale_input refusal never shows a mixed pack and is acceptable. A research squad assesses whether artifact-level mutex locking is needed.

options: Only when a deny entry keeps T out
payload.question: Does an active enhancer alone satisfy a required T whatever keeps T out of force?

options: Leave writes unchanged here; follow-up issue
Change the write rule in this mission
payload.question: Should the write rule allow a deny on a required T when an active override/enhancement of it is in force?

payload.final_answer: No. Enhancers always require their T to be active in order to work; they do not stand on their own. A required T is satisfied only by T itself or an active override of it; an enhancer never satisfies it, and an enhancer whose T is not active has no effect.
Relax it in this mission, override only: a deny on a required T is accepted when an active override of T is in force and T is not locked. Overrides are not permitted on locked artifacts.

options: Enhancer rule wins: not in force, reported
payload.question: A required or locked artifact that is an enhancer whose target is not in force: in force or not?

payload.final_answer: Merged edges
Enhancer rule wins: not in force, reported as required-but-ungrounded

payload.question: A1 preset shadowing

payload.final_answer: Required = union of the must-have items of every governing copy of a preset id; requirements only tighten.

payload.question: A2 requirement checked once

payload.final_answer: Iterate the requirement check to a fixed point on the final set; cycles among required artifacts/overriders are refused or reported.

payload.question: A3 override chains

payload.final_answer: Overrides compose transitively top to bottom: F overrides E overrides T leaves F in force; F hides E and T and satisfies a requirement on T (F -> T).

payload.question: A4 GET->PUT round trip

payload.final_answer: A full replace judges the floor only on deny entries it adds, and also drops ids the packs no longer hold, reporting them, instead of 422.

payload.question: A5 registration impact

payload.final_answer: Registration runs an impact check over every closure the pack joins (locks/mutability, override cycles, floor), naming the packs; the endpoint is asynchronous by design: accept the request (202) and hand a callback/status URI the client uses to learn when registration completed.

payload.question: A6 extendable vs overrides edge

payload.final_answer: Same gate for both override paths: only open artifacts can be overridden; an overrides edge onto an extendable or locked target is refused at registration and not applied at read.

payload.question: A7 mission types and activatedKinds

payload.final_answer: Mission types, steps and agent profiles follow the same activation and override/enhancement rules as any artifact; activatedKinds is a remnant of core, not a domain rule; revise the API/representation if needed; an architecture/analysis/code-shape squad assesses it.

payload.question: A8 enhancer cycles

payload.final_answer: Refuse enhances cycles outright; an enhancement can never exist in isolation and must always link to a real (non-enhancer) artifact.

payload.question: A10 required id no pack holds

payload.final_answer: Other packs' preset items count as inbound references (DELETE refused 409), and must-have items no pack holds are dropped from the floor and reported.

payload.question: A11/A12 dual edge and self-override

payload.final_answer: Refuse at registration (422) an artifact that both enhances and overrides one target, and an overrides edge that resolves to itself.

payload.question: A13 deactivate as inverse

payload.final_answer: Accept and document: a cascading deactivate removes t and what its walk reaches unless something else active keeps it; prior selections are not remembered.

payload.question: A14 sibling enhancers

payload.final_answer: enhances does not count as a sibling conflict; a settlement names exactly one winner.

payload.question: A15 policy lock scope

payload.final_answer: A pack may lock and enforce artifacts of the packs it builds on (enterprise enforcement); scope is the pack and its depends_on/lineage ancestors, not unrelated packs that share the closure.

payload.question: B1 version pins

payload.final_answer: Writes drop unsatisfiable version pins and report them in dropped; keep a per-pack version->content-digest history so a version can never be reused with other content; reads report an unheld pin in the skipped report.

payload.question: B2 eager stale drop

payload.final_answer: Keep: stale ids drop on any write, reported in dropped.

payload.question: B3 delete deadlocks

payload.final_answer: Whole-pack replace checks references against the new tree; every 409 lists the referring artifacts and packs.

payload.question: B4 silent floor changes

payload.final_answer: Registration status reports floor/lock changes and the activations whose in-force set changes; GET /activations/{id} carries a marker when deny entries are not applied.

payload.question: B5 includeDeactivated and ancestors

payload.final_answer: Clear deny entries only on artifacts the walk reaches and selects, not on lineage ancestors it passes through.

payload.question: B6/B7 write warnings

payload.final_answer: ActivationChange carries a warnings list (e.g. enhanced_target_not_in_force, kind_not_activated) so a write predicts the read.

payload.question: B8 own lock

payload.final_answer: A pack's own policy does not bind the pack itself; it protects its artifacts from other packs.

payload.question: A7 Q1 mission type cascade

payload.final_answer: Selecting a mission type cascades to the steps it holds (like requires); steps stay bound to it (in force only while it is). W32 withdrawn.

payload.question: A7 Q2 mission type deny

payload.final_answer: Uniform: mission types are deniable via deactivated.mission_type unless required or locked; floor and locks apply as to any kind.

payload.question: A7 Q3 preset kind exclusions

payload.final_answer: Drop the skill/glossary_pack exclusion: a preset may name any kind; one kind registry everywhere.

payload.question: A7 Q4 activatedKinds/missionTypes on writes

payload.final_answer: Refuse now: activatedKinds and missionTypes on activation writes answer 422; core must regenerate first. Stored documents upgrade to schemaVersion 2 on read.

payload.question: Slice A0 placement

payload.final_answer: A0 (built-behaviour changes + IC-20 kind model) is its own PR stacked on #399, before PR A.

payload.question: Required/locked artifact bound to a mission type not in force

payload.final_answer: Drop and report (required-but-not-in-force), like the floor enhancer without a target.

payload.question: When is a v1 activation document upgraded

payload.final_answer: On the next write; reads upgrade in memory only and never write.

payload.question: v1 to v2 upgrade: selections outside the never-enforced activatedKinds gate

payload.final_answer: Keep every selection; drop the gate. The gate had no observable effect (reads 501, writes ignored it), so the upgrade changes nothing the user saw.

payload.question: SkippedReport.skippedByScope after IC-20

payload.final_answer: Keep it: it is the write report of the cascade scope (CascadeRules, ActivationChangeMapper, activation-selections.feature), live in #399. Only the read-side kind-gate meaning goes; at read it is always empty, like unreachedBehindDeactivated and skippedShared.

payload.question: NFR-003/NFR-008 failing gate

payload.final_answer: The build-failing gate is a deterministic operation-count budget in check (one compose per read, walk node visits bounded by the closure size, one in-force resolution per write); wall time is measured in timingBudgets and reported at 1x and 3x, report-only per ADR-0057 (runner variance ~2x). The NFR-008 end state (registration_timed_out at 60 s + 30 s) is a deterministic fake-clock test.

payload.question: version_not_held on create vs the B1 write-time drop

payload.final_answer: createActivation keeps 422 version_not_held for a pin in its own body that no pack satisfies (input error, nothing stored yet); replace and the per-artifact and preset writes drop an unsatisfiable pin into ActivationChange.dropped (B1).

payload.question: Where the FR-042 round trip runs

payload.final_answer: Two tests: client-java captures the wire body of a GET then PUT with a JDK HttpServer (no new dependency) and asserts absent lists stay absent or are sent as []; the server side canonicalizes an empty list and an absent member to one stored form (WP03), pinned by an @contract scenario in deployable: PUT of the client's body keeps the ETag and the stored bytes.

payload.question: git >= 2.50.1 in tests

payload.final_answer: Real-git tests carry the tag git-host, are excluded from check and PIT, and run in a dedicated CI job that asserts git --version >= 2.50.1 first; locally they are reported not run, never passed. check uses a fake git shim (a script on a test PATH) for GitCommand, the version check and NFR-011.

payload.question: Two required artifacts overriding each other (A2)

payload.final_answer: An override cycle is refused: 422 override_cycle at registration (C28) and 500 pack_unreadable at read when the cycle forms among base plus unsatisfied required artifacts; never a loop, never a partial answer.

payload.question: What counts as red-first evidence for a contract scenario

payload.final_answer: Only an assertion failure with every step bound (a wrong status or body). Undefined or pending steps are not red: a suite guard fails the run on any UNDEFINED or PENDING step. Contract WPs commit their scenarios tagged @WIP (excluded); the serving WP binds the glue, records the red assertion failure, then removes @WIP.
